candidate_relations.reason: Infectious meningitis from Enterococcus gallinarum is a translocation manifestation of hyperinfection, not disseminated strongyloidiasis itself.
SLE with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage was the initial clinical diagnosis and conflicts with disseminated strongyloidiasis after intensive immunosuppression.
Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is a pulmonary manifestation/complication, not the disseminated strongyloidiasis diagnosis.
Systemic lupus erythematosus is the underlying disease treated with cyclophosphamide and high-dose steroids, not disseminated strongyloidiasis.
Henoch-Schönlein purpura is a different small-vessel vasculitis and does not explain enteric meningitis plus DAH after immunosuppression.
Coccidioidal meningitis is a different fungal meningitis; CSF grew Enterococcus gallinarum.
Toxoplasmosis is a different opportunistic infection, not disseminated strongyloidiasis.
Systemic vasculitis is a different inflammatory diagnosis, not strongyloidiasis.
SLE flare conflicts with absent lupus activity signs and with disseminated strongyloidiasis after intensification of immunosuppression.
Neurobrucellosis is a different zoonotic meningitis, not disseminated strongyloidiasis.
Infective endocarditis is a different endovascular infection not supported on this record.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate names disseminated strongyloidiasis; the record describes steroid-treated SLE with enteric meningitis, DAH, and purpura but no parasitology.
